results.title: Cottage cheese pie recipe: precise cooling requirements for perfect slice structural stability
results.description: The structure of this cottage cheese pie relies on a fundamental contrast between a crumbly, short-crust base and a dense, custard-like filling. The defining characteristic of the pastry is its tenderness, which is achieved through the specific state of the fat and the method of incorporation. The Role of Temperature and Texture The decisive action in this recipe is the use of frozen butter (125g) grated directly into a mixture of 1 cup of wheat flour, 2 tablespoons of sugar, 1 teaspoon of baking powder, and a pinch of salt. By keeping the butter frozen and rubbing it quickly by hand into the dry ingredients, the baker prevents the fat from emulsifying with the flour. This creates a "rubbed-in" texture-a coarse crumb-rather than a cohesive dough. This specific state ensures that the pastry remains tender and flaky rather than tough or bread-like after it hits the 180°C oven. Filling Stability and Assembly While the crust provides the architecture, the filling is governed by the binding properties of 2 egg yolks. The mixture of 350g of cottage cheese, 1.2 cups of sugar, and 1.2 teaspoons of vanilla extract must be worked with a fork until homogeneous. The yolks act as the primary stabilizer, transforming the cottage cheese into a smooth mass that can support the weight of the topping without collapsing.

results.title: Vivani Medical Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Update
results.description: Top-line results for SLIM-1™, the first-in-human Phase 1 trial of NPM-139, Vivani's miniature, ultra-long-acting semaglutide implant under development for chronic weight management, are anticipated for announcement later this week Cortigent-ClearOne merger is awaiting final regulatory approvals allowing establishment of Cortigent as a standalone company trading on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol CRGT ALAMEDA, Calif., Nov. 11, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Vivani Medical, Inc. (Nasdaq: VANI) ("Vivani" or the "Company"), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing miniature, ultra-long-acting drug implants utilizing its proprietary NanoPortal™ technology, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided a business update. "The third quarter and recent weeks mark a period of strong progress and forward momentum for Vivani” said Adam Mendelsohn, PhD, CEO of the Company. "The top-line SLIM-1 results will be announced this week. We look forward to sharing those results with shareholders, industry peers, and the broader community of physicians and patients seeking less frequent dosing and the promise of potential improvements in convenience, medication adherence, and tolerability associated with GLP-1 therapies on the market and in clinical-stage development." Dr. Mendelsohn continued: "Roughly half of patients don’t take their medications for chronic diseases as prescribed, and GLP-1 therapies are no exception. With NPM-139, we are designing a novel GLP-1 therapy that a patient could receive once or twice a year during a routine primary care visit. Another key feature afforded by our unique NanoPortal implant technology is the ability to provide an "off-ramp” when discontinuation of therapy is warranted for example when a woman becomes pregnant or there is an aspiration risk during surgery. While there are multiple GLP-1 injectable candidates targeting monthly or quarterly administration under development, none can offer reversibility comparable to our NanoPortal implants. We strongly believe this could be an important consideration for the more than 20% of current GLP-1 users who are women of child-bearing potential.” Recent Business Highlights On October 30, 2026, the Company filed an current report on Form 8-K with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to clarify that the expected close of the of the Cortigent merger remains subject to final regulatory approval and is expected to close shortly after approval is received. On August 6, 2026, Vivani announced full enrollment and successful initial dosing of all participants in its SLIM-1™ Phase 1 trial for NPM-139, a miniature, subdermal semaglutide implant being designed to provide six- to twelve-months of continuous drug delivery utilizing our proprietary NanoPortal™ technology. The trial of 20 GLP-1 naïve participants in Australia includes low-doses of NPM-139 and Wegovy® to assess safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics. Changes in weight were measured. Top-Line results from the SLIM-1 trial are anticipated to be announced later this week. On July 7, 2026, the Company announced the signing of a new agreement with Novo Nordisk, now known as Novo, to evaluate NPM-139, the Company’s semaglutide drug implant. NPM-139 is under development for chronic weight management. There are no exclusivity provisions for NPM-139, or Vivani’s proprietary NanoPortal technology associated with this agreement. On July 2, 2026, Vivani announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement and plan of merger (the "Agreement”) among its wholly owned subsidiary Cortigent Inc., ClearOne, Inc., a Nasdaq-listed company, and a wholly owned subsidiary of ClearOne ("MergerSub”), pursuant to which Cortigent will become a wholly owned subsidiary of ClearOne upon consummation. In connection with the transaction, ClearOne is pursuing a financing which aims to raise $10 million to $15 million concurrently with the merger’s closing. Upcoming Anticipated Milestones Release of top-line data for SLIM-1, the on-going Phase 1 study of low-dose NPM-139, Vivani’s miniature, ultra long-acting semaglutide implant under development for chronic weight management, are anticipated in November 2026. Preparation, and submission of an Investigational New Drug ("IND”) Application for NPM-139 to support initiation of a proposed Phase 2 dose-ranging study of this semaglutide implant is planned for 2027. The transition of Cortigent into an independent, publicly traded company shortly after receiving final regulatory approval and completion of all closing and related financing activities. Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results Cash: As of September 30, 2026, Vivani had cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash totaling $15.5 million, compared to $20.8 million as of June 30, 2026. Research and development expense, net: Research and development expense, net of grants, during the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $5.0 million, compared to $4.5 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase of $0.5 million, or 11%, was primarily attributable to an increase in the clinical trial related expense from our Biopharm Division. General and administrative expense, net: General and administrative expense, net of grants, during the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $2.5 million, compared to $2.2 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase of $0.3 million, or 14%, was primarily attributable to an increase in personnel and related expenses from our Neurostimulation Division and our Biopharm Division. Other income, net: Other income, net during the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $0.3 million, compared to $0.2 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase of $0.1 million was primarily attributable to amounts recognized under the Australian R&D Tax Incentive Program and higher interest income earned during the period. Net loss: For the foregoing reasons, we had a net loss of $7.3 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $6.5 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025. About SLIM-1™ Trial SLIM-1 is an open-label, active-controlled trial evaluating a low-dose NPM-139 (semaglutide implant) given to 10 participants, and the starting dose of Wegovy (0.25mg/week semaglutide injection) given to 10 participants, over a four-week duration. The trial was designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetic profile in overweight or obese participants who are otherwise healthy. Changes in weight were also measured. Top-line results from SLIM-1 are anticipated to be released later this week. About Vivani Medical, Inc. Leveraging its proprietary NanoPortal™ platform, Vivani develops miniature, biopharmaceutical implants designed to deliver drug molecules steadily over extended periods of time with the goal of guaranteeing adherence and improving patient tolerance to their medication. Vivani is developing a portfolio of GLP-1 based implants for metabolic diseases including obesity and type 2 diabetes. These NanoPortal implants are designed for once- or twice-yearly administration to provide patients with the opportunity to realize the full potential benefit of their medication by avoiding the numerous challenges associated with the daily or weekly administration of orals and injectables, including tolerability issues and loss of efficacy. Medication non-adherence occurs when patients do not take their medication as prescribed. This affects an alarming number of patients, approximately 50%, including those taking daily pills. For more information, please visit: www.vivani.com. About Cortigent, Inc. Cortigent, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Vivani, is developing brain implant devices to help patients recover critical body functions. Its patent-protected precision neurostimulation technology platform leverages neuroscience and proprietary microelectronics to create advanced medical devices. Vivani’s predecessor, Second Sight Medical Products, previously marketed Argus® II, the first and only medical device to obtain FDA approval to treat a rare form of blindness. This innovative device has helped hundreds of profoundly blind patients to achieve meaningful visual perception. Cortigent’s next generation investigational system, the Orion® cortical stimulation system, has been designed to treat blindness caused by common conditions including glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy. Orion has an FDA Breakthrough Device designation, completed a 6-year Early Feasibility Study in 2025 with promising safety and efficacy results and is covered by an extensive intellectual property estate. Cortigent is also applying its core technology to improving recovery of arm and hand motion in patients with paralysis due to stroke. For more information and patient videos, please visit: www.cortigent.com. results.title: Mid-Season Highs & Lows
results.description: We are halfway through the season, and our Bills are 7-1 for the first time since 1993. Sounds like a reason to celebrate. I thought at best the Bills would be 6-2 at this point, at worst 5-3. Joe Brady has answered the call and Josh Allen and the offense are humming right along, it hasn't always been pretty, but when the game is on the line and the Bills need to score, I feel confident that the Bills can score at any moment. The defense, as expected, is a work-in-progress. Giving up lots of points early was concerning. Have these last two games shown that the defense is turning things around? We shall see. Especially now that we've added Amani Hooker. I wanted to get your thoughts on the highs and lows of the team. Highs: Tyler Bass. His kicks can still be entertaining, but give this guy credit, he has rebounded in a big way. Bravo, Bass-O-Matic! Keon Coleman: He is not a #1 WR, but his play has been tremendous. Little to complain about. Greg Rousseau: This is an easy choice, but seeing Groot play the way he has consistently, has been amazing. DJ Moore: When he's on the field, he is a difference maker. Josh Allen: Another obvious choice, but he is the team, a star. He does make some odd decisions, but when the game is on the line, we can count on him. Ty Johnson: He still is a great option as a running back & receiver. James Cook: The fumbles have been rough however he is our top runner and he's always giving his all. Watching how shifty he is and how he can break through the line is fantastic. Deone Walker & Ed Oliver: They may not get a ton of stats, but they are monsters. Christian Benford: Struggled early, but has come back strong after his injury, and is showing why he's our top Cornerback. Davison Igbinosun: By far our top rookie. Had some penalty issues, but he looks very comfortable in coverage, and has been a good defender. Joe Brady: Some cute and questionable playcalling still happens, but he does play to the strengths of the offense. I also appreciate how he treated James Cook during his fumbling issues. Instead of having him sit on the sidelines for a quarter, he showed how much he trusted him by sending him back out there. Starting Offensive Line: Not much to complain about with this group. Halftime Adjustments: Whatever they are feeding the team at halftime, keep giving it to them. Lows: Penalties: Crazy amount early this season. This has to be fixed. CJ Gardner-Johnson: I really thought he would be the leader in our secondary. Joshua Palmer: I thought we would see a rebound from this guy. Michael Hoecht: I guess this is what happens to a player after an achilles injury. Aside from being a Special Teams demon, he's done little. Javon Solomon: Yes, he's not a starter, but this is his third season with the team, and all I see is a Special Teamer. Jackson Hawes: Penalties have been a killer for him. Definitely has taken a step back. That's how I see it. What's your takeaway?
